articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License, Issues New FAQ
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued an amended Venezuela-related General License and a new Frequently Asked Question (FAQ) on October 16, 2026.
This action updates the existing sanctions framework concerning Venezuela, providing further guidance and potentially adjusting authorized activities within the sanctioned economy.
The specific details of the amendments and the new FAQ are available on the Treasury Department's website, impacting entities and individuals engaged in Venezuela-related transactions.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iran-Related and Cuba Entities, Issues New General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and a Cuba designation on October 15, 2026.

These actions include the addition of 16 individuals and 11 entities to the Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, targeting financial institutions, currency exchange firms, and energy and trading companies.

Notably, Cuba's Banco Internacional de Comercio S.A. (BICSA) was designated due to its ties with Iran's Karafarin Bank, which has been under sanctions since 2020. OFAC also issued new and amended General Licenses and Frequently Asked Questions to accompany these designations.

articles.headline: OFAC Removes Venezuela-Related Designation
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a Venezuela-related designation removal on October 14, 2026.
This action indicates a change in the sanctions status for a specific entity or individual previously designated under the Venezuela sanctions program.
Further details regarding the identity of the removed party and the implications of this action are available through official OFAC channels.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) implemented new designations related to counter narcotics and counter terrorism efforts on October 13, 2026.
These designations target individuals and entities involved in illicit activities that pose a threat to U.S. national security and foreign policy.
The action underscores the U.S. government's ongoing commitment to disrupting global illicit finance networks associated with drug trafficking and terrorism.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Settlement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics, Issues ICC Designation and Burma Removal
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics on October 9, 2026, alongside an International Criminal Court (ICC) designation and a Burma-related designation removal.
The settlement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics addresses apparent violations of OFAC sanctions programs, with the company agreeing to pay a penalty of $175,015.

Additionally, OFAC issued General License 12 related to the International Criminal Court, authorizing the settlement of transactions involving certain blocked persons, and removed a Burma-related designation.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Russia-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued a new Russia-related General License on October 9, 2026.
This new license authorizes certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited under the Russia sanctions program.
The issuance of General Licenses provides specific exemptions to sanctions, allowing for particular activities to proceed under defined conditions.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iran-Related Entities, Amends Russia-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and issued an Iran-related General License on October 8, 2026.
Concurrently, OFAC issued an amended Russia-related General License, indicating adjustments to existing authorizations under the Russia sanctions program.
These actions are part of ongoing efforts to address threats posed by Iran and to refine the implementation of sanctions against Russia.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Global Sanctions and Export Controls Blog

articles.headline: OFAC Publishes Iran-Related Alert and Amended FAQ, Removes Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) published an Iran-related Alert and an amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ) on October 5, 2026.
The Alert warns foreign financial institutions (FFIs) that transacting with sanctioned Iranian financial institutions could lead to targeting without advance notification.
OFAC also announced designations removals and updates, indicating adjustments to its sanctions lists.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Global Sanctions and Export Controls Blog

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new counter terrorism designations on October 2, 2026.
These designations target individuals and entities identified as supporting terrorist activities globally.
The action reinforces the U.S. government's commitment to combating terrorism financing and disrupting networks that facilitate such activities.

articles.headline: Bank of America Fined $11,662,930 by OFAC for Sanctions Violations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Bank of America, N.A., resulting in a civil monetary penalty of $11,662,930.
This penalty is part of a broader enforcement action by the U.S. Department of the Treasury, which also included significant fines from FinCEN and the OCC.

The violations involved apparent breaches of multiple sanctions programs, including those related to Iran, Russia, narcotics, and global terrorism, due to failures in correspondent banking, watchlist updates, and handling of blocked persons' accounts.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
